definitions.explanation: A building method in which the structural frame is made of steel. A standard category in Japanese real-estate listings, often abbreviated S{造|ぞう}.

examples.japanese: このビルは{鉄骨造|てっこつぞう}だ。
{鉄骨造|てっこつぞう}のアパートを{探|さが}している。
examples.english: I'm looking for a steel-framed apartment.

examples.japanese: {木造|もくぞう}よりも{鉄骨造|てっこつぞう}のほうが{防音性|ぼうおんせい}が{高|たか}いと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: Steel-frame construction is said to have better soundproofing than wooden construction.

notes:
Formed from {鉄骨|てっこつ} (steel frame) + {造|ぞう} (construction, build). One of the main structural categories listed when renting or buying property in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鉄骨造|てっこつぞう}のマンション: a steel-frame apartment building
- {軽量|けいりょう}{鉄骨造|てっこつぞう}: light-gauge steel construction

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {木造|もくぞう}: wooden construction — frame built of wood; generally cheaper but less soundproof
- {鉄筋|てっきん}コンクリート{造|ぞう}: reinforced-concrete construction — uses steel-reinforced concrete; more durable and soundproof than steel-frame alone
